messages:
Lin (Support): Hey team — customer reported p95 for /v1/generate jumped from ~120ms to ~480ms starting ~08:12 UTC. They see user-facing slowdowns. No 5xx, mostly higher tail latency. Can SRE confirm?
Sara (SRE): On it. Which customer and region?
Lin (Support): acme-inc, us-west-2. They attached times and a few trace ids: trace: a1b2c3d4, a1b2c3d5.
Sara (SRE): grabbing traces, also pulling p95 from dashboards now.
OpsBot: New deployment to runtime-group-3 completed at 08:05 UTC (deploy-2026-03-14-3f2a).
Mike (Runtime): that deploy touched batching changes and default kv-cache TTL. Posting the PR: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/512
Leo (Observability): quick heads-up — two dashboards show different p95 deltas. svc-latency-panel shows jump to 480ms at 08:10; p95-rollup-panel shows only 170ms. Might be different aggregation windows.
Sara (SRE): that matches what I'm seeing. Support timeline aligns with the deploy. Strange the panel disagreement though.
Leo (Observability): likely cause: one panel is computing histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le)) and the other is using quantile_over_time(0.95, http_request_duration_seconds{endpoint="/v1/generate"}[5m]). Different semantics. Also one dashboard includes synthetic/health-check routes in the metric.
Mike (Runtime): can we get raw samples for the customer traffic? I want to see per-request timing distribution and whether KV cache misses spiked.
Sara (SRE): running a small extraction against our request log store for acme-inc, timeframe 08:00-08:30. Command: 
```bash
python infra/tools/latency_extract.py --customer acme-inc --start 2026-03-14T08:00:00Z --end 2026-03-14T08:30:00Z --out /tmp/acme_latencies.csv
```
Sara (SRE): output shows p50 90ms, p95 470ms, p99 890ms for that window. Raw samples confirm tail spike.
Lin (Support): customer also says their traffic pattern increased concurrency at 08:06 due to a batch job. Maybe combined with runtime change.
Mike (Runtime): PR changed continuous batching heuristics — if more concurrent requests, batch size grew and CPU contention sometimes caused higher per-request latency for small requests. I can roll back that tweak if needed.
Leo (Observability): digging into histogram bucket boundaries — I found that dashboard A (svc-latency-panel) uses buckets: [0.001,0.005,0.01,0.05,0.1,0.2,0.5,1] while rollup panel uses aggregated internal summaries that re-bucket to coarse percentiles. That causes the histogram_quantile to be noisier at tails when bucket boundaries misalign.
Sara (SRE): so the disagreement is: one query uses raw bucketed histogram (accurate for distribution shape) and the other uses stored rollup summaries that approximate quantiles differently. Which one do we trust for root-cause?
Leo (Observability): trust raw samples and raw histogram_quantile for now. Rollups are useful for long-term trends but they smooth tails.
Mike (Runtime): immediate mitigation: revert batching heuristic and reduce max batch size to previous safe value. I can cut a hotfix. Any objections?
Sara (SRE): do it. Also, set a temporary alert: fire if p95 > 300ms for 2 consecutive 1m windows for /v1/generate.
Lin (Support): I'll tell the customer we're rolling back a runtime tweak and monitoring, ETA 10m.
OpsBot: Incident created: INC-2026-314-01 - p95 regression - assigned to Sara, Mike.
Leo (Observability): action items for me: 1) align both dashboards to use the same source (raw histogram buckets) and add a note in panel explaining differences; 2) add a saved query to compare rollup vs raw quantiles over selectable windows.
Sara (SRE): I captured traces for the two sample trace ids. For trace a1b2c3d4, span timings show Redis KV cache miss on token lookup at +120ms and then scheduling delay; for a1b2c3d5 it was cache hit. So cache miss + larger batches amplified tail.
Mike (Runtime): that suggests two orthogonal contributors: (1) batching heuristic increase due to higher concurrency which increases QUEUE latencies, (2) kv-cache TTL change causing more cold misses. I'll roll back batching tweak and revert kv-cache TTL to previous value. Pushing hotfix now.
Sara (SRE): rollback in progress. OpsBot, watch deploy health.
OpsBot: Hotfix rollback deployed to runtime-group-3 at 08:22 UTC.
Sara (SRE): post-rollback numbers (08:25-08:30): p50 95ms, p95 155ms, p99 310ms for acme-inc window — tail substantially reduced.
Lin (Support): customer confirms perceived latency normalized. Thanks.
Mike (Runtime): I'll open a follow-up PR with more conservative batching thresholds and add telemetry for queue lengths and batch sizes per-second so this doesn't surprise us.
Leo (Observability): follow-ups from observability side: add a dashboard note and an onboarding doc section about how different quantile computations can diverge and recommended queries to use for incident triage.
Sara (SRE): closing loop: root cause = combination of batching heuristic + transient KV cache miss spike under higher concurrency. Disagreement in dashboards caused confusion because one panel used aggregated rollups instead of raw histogram buckets.
Lin (Support): final message to customer drafted: "We rolled back a runtime change and reverted cache TTL; latency should be back to normal. We're adding telemetry and safer batching thresholds to prevent recurrence." I'll send that now. :white_check_mark:
Mike (Runtime): thanks all. Owners: Mike -> runtime fixes, Leo -> dashboard alignment, Sara -> postmortem + alerts, Lin -> customer comms.
Sara (SRE): creating postmortem draft and linking traces/queries. Will ping when ready.
Leo (Observability): adding the saved queries now; linking them in the postmortem.
Sara (SRE): marking incident resolved pending postmortem.
Lin (Support): marking customer case resolved.
